note_sections.t: Clinical reassessment sought after mpMRI acquisition and a PSA increase reaching 24.0 ng/mL.

A 68-year-old mechanical engineer initiated evaluation in September 2022 due to an elevated PSA reading. He is a non-smoker, and his prior biopsy bucket remains None. Long-standing hypertension is managed with metoprolol, while osteoarthritis discomfort is addressed with paracetamol taken only when necessary. He shares a home with his wife, and adult offspring stop by every week, with their son handling administrative correspondence. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms produce an IPSS total of 12. A stable cardiology assessment occurred during autumn 2024, accompanied by routine thyroid and vascular checks. Joint stiffness limits his mobility, necessitating a walking frame for extended distances and a ground-floor consultation room. He explicitly denies unexplained weight loss, osseous pain, or nocturnal diaphoresis.

DRE — texture: symmetrically smooth; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: absent. The glandular surface presents without palpable nodules, aligning with a normal digital examination. General inspection notes a well-nourished individual in no acute distress, registering a BMI of 26.0. Hemodynamic parameters remain stable at 130/73 mmHg with a regular pulse of 68 bpm. Cardiovascular and respiratory auscultation yield unremarkable results.
